model.notes: Side is inferred from book_rules.fav_bp (negative = short). The rules concentrate on one mechanism, momentum still live at entry under a tight floor, with leverage, 1h direction and name floor history as the separating conditions. A 1h rollover (1h clearly negative) separated the winning pump-fade shorts from the floored ones. I avoided long-side and post-crash rules because outcomes there were mixed in this week's reviews.

accepted_now: Skip shorts into a pump that is still accelerating: 4h move at least +10% and the last hour still up at least 1%.
Skip high-leverage shorts on names where the book already hit the floor in a large share of past positions.
Skip 20x+ shorts on names already up 15% or more in 24h.
Skip shorts when the 1h bounce is strong (3% or more) and Bybit longs are below 0.45.
Skip shorts into a pump that is still running hard: last hour up 3% or more and 4h up 5% or more, at any leverage.
Skip 10x+ shorts on names up 20% or more in 24h when the book has already floored on a large share of past entries in that name.
Skip 20x+ shorts on names up 20% or more in 24h unless the last hour is already down at least 2%.

new.why: Pump already happened (4h up >6%), buying burst has faded and OI is unwinding: late longs exiting, so shorting the exhausted top should lower adverse excursion versus entering at the signal hour.
Price ran against the signal (better short price), but taker flow has turned to selling and the crowd is not adding shorts. The squeeze risk is spent, so a 5% stop rarely hits the winners.
Positive funding means longs pay and are crowded. A 1h up-move on below-normal trade activity is a weak, thin rally, which makes a good fade entry for shorts.
Long-heavy crowd starts unwinding (OI falling, price turning down): a long liquidation cascade begins, so the short enters with momentum and little adverse excursion, which suits a tight 3% stop.

patterns.notes: Focus is on exhaustion-after-pump and long-unwind states to reduce adverse excursion. Exits combine the book's own exit with moderate stops (3-5%), since the path data shows 1-2% stops cut most winners.
